summary: Advice requested: prevent 429s when concurrent low-latency websockets and large embedding backfills overlap
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports frequent 429 responses on short-lived websocket chat sessions while a nightly embedding backfill runs. The 429s are concentrated at stream startup and lead to visible reconnects for end users.

Impact: Interactive product search and chat display transient failures during business hours, while embeddings finish with extended retry delays. Business impact: degraded user experience and longer data pipeline windows.

Environment: Dedicated GPU pool, production, us-east. Chat clients use multiplexed WebSocket connections (SDK v1.20). Backfill uses 48 parallel workers, HTTP/2, batch size 400. Customer recently reduced overall tenant quota after onboarding a new sub-tenant.

Steps customer uses to reproduce: 1) Open 120 short-lived websocket sessions that connect, send a 1-2 token prompt and close within 8-15 seconds. 2) Start embedding backfill concurrently. 3) Observe X-RateLimit headers and 429 responses from both chat and embeddings routes during overlap.

Observed evidence: Console shows tenant-level short-window bucket becomes zero during overlap. Rate-limit headers on 429s include remaining=0 and reset in ~12s. Embedding workers report exponential-backoff retries which succeed. No 5xx errors observed.

Customer expectation: Short-lived interactive streams should be insulated from bulk ingestion bursts or have a prioritized burst allowance so user-facing streams maintain low failure rates.
comments: 2026-03-14 - Diego Rivera: Opened ticket after observing morning support queue spike with reports of chat reconnects. Asked if there are recommended config changes to avoid rescheduling backfills.

2026-03-14 - Nina Patel (Support): Acknowledged and requested rate-limit headers, sample stack traces from workers, and exact client concurrency numbers. Suggested temporary mitigations while we investigate.
2026-03-15 - Diego Rivera: Uploaded archived headers and a timeline CSV of job start/stop. Confirmed API keys are long-lived; no ephemeral keys used.
investigation_notes: Reproduced in staging using a tenant with identical quota profile and a dedicated pool. Replayed workload: 120 short ws sessions + 48 embedding workers. Tenant short-window (10s) token bucket depleted rapidly and produced 429s across routes.

Rate-limiter architecture: tenant-level enforcement includes a short burst window (10s) and a smoothing window (60s). Per-route weights exist but default weights did not protect chat from high-volume bulk writes.

Findings: route accounting charges both websocket and embedding traffic to the tenant short-window bucket by default. High instantaneous token consumption from embeddings within the 10s window starves short-lived streams.
No evidence of SDK double-posting or proxy miscount. Clock skew checks passed. Dedicated pool had no low-latency reservation configured for chat traffic.
resolution_notes: Short-term recommendations provided to customer: 1) Reduce embedding worker parallelism to 24 and decrease batch size to 200 during business hours. 2) Apply client-side jittered exponential backoff for retries. 3) Temporary increase of tenant short-window burst quota by 25% via console for a 48 hour window.

Long-term guidance: 1) Configure an isolated per-route quota for 'chat.realtime' with a dedicated short-window token-bucket and higher weight to protect interactive flows. 2) Enable dedicated-pool reservation for realtime traffic to guarantee capacity. 3) Consider issuing ephemeral keys for interactive clients so route-level policies can be applied without affecting ingestion keys. 4) Adjust embedding route smoothing to use a 60s window to reduce microbursts.

Action items: 1) Support to send a route-fencing playbook and sample console configs. 2) Schedule a tenant configuration review with Solutions Engineering to set up route isolation and dedicated reservations if customer wants assisted rollout.
workaround: Temporarily reduce embedding parallelism and batch size during peak hours, enable jittered retries, and request a short-term increase to the tenant short-window burst via console.
